checked.claim: TikTok: DPC decision 30 April 2025 (485m + 45m) plus suspension order; High Court stay; Supreme Court 30 April 2026 dismissed DPC appeal; mid-2026 High Court upheld findings, sent suspension order back; fine-size appeal undecided
checked.evidence: DPC fines page dates the decision 30/04/2025, EUR 530m, Pending Appeal. Irish Times 30 Apr 2026: Supreme Court unanimously dismissed the DPC's appeal, stay test is one of national law. Acompli/Freevacy (published 11 June 2026): High Court judgment of 3 June 2026 largely upheld the Art. 46 and Art. 13 findings and directed the DPC to reconsider the suspension order; the court would consider the appeal on the amount separately. Irish Times 30 June 2026: a separate judgment on the fine amount had been circulated to the parties and would be published later. 'Mid-2026' is vague and 'still to be decided' is out of date.
checked.replacement: DPC decision of 30 April 2025 (EUR 485m transfers, EUR 45m transparency) plus a transfer suspension order. The High Court stayed it; the Supreme Court (30 April 2026) dismissed the DPC's appeal on the stay test. In June 2026 the High Court upheld the infringement findings but sent the suspension order back to the DPC. A separate judgment on the size of the fine was circulated to the parties at the end of June 2026; its outcome had not been published at last report.

notes: Most serious issue: the TikTok case summary is stale. The High Court ruled on the merits on 3 June 2026 (per Acompli; Freevacy published 11 June), and by 30 June a separate judgment on the fine amount had been circulated to the parties. The confidence line should drop 'the exact date of the 2026 High Court TikTok judgment'. s.150(7) lets a complainant appeal if the Commission fails to meet the required timelines. That is a statutory hook for appeal.inaction, which the file currently says is unconfirmed; worth stating. Minor: the Meta EUR 1.2bn decision is dated 12 May 2023 but was announced on 22 May 2023, which is the date most readers know. The DPC fines table, as WebFetch summarised it, also lists an HSE EUR 65,000 fine dated 18/08/2020, separate from the 2026 one; no conflict.
